title: Carnian Pluvial Episode
summary: The Carnian Pluvial Episode, around 234 to 232 million years ago in the Late Triassic, was a time of rising global humidity and temperature linked to volcanism in the Wrangellia large igneous province. Pulses of carbon-depleted CO2 are tied to negative carbon-isotope shifts and wetter conditions. The Dolomites of Italy hold an age-constrained record with plant turnover and the oldest fossil amber, and the episode is linked to dinosaur and conifer diversification.

uncertainty.note: Roghi et al. (2022) give around 234 to 232 Ma; Lu et al. (2021) give ca. 234.0 to 232.4 Ma in the Jiyuan Basin, North China, with U-Pb zircon ages of 233.1 ± 1.3 and 232.9 ± 2.1 Ma. Years are Ma counted back from the present.

where.modern_name: Dolomites, Italy (reference section; the episode is global and linked to Wrangellia volcanism in western North America)
where.historical_name: Dolomites area on the western Tethys margin of Pangaea; no polities exist at this date

importance.justification: A global climate shift coinciding with turnover in land plants and the rise of dinosaurs.

sources.title: An Exceptionally Preserved Terrestrial Record of LIP Effects on Plants in the Carnian (Upper Triassic) Amber-Bearing Section of the Dolomites, Italy (Frontiers in Earth Science 10:900586)

reviewer_note: Least sure of the pin: the episode is global, so the Dolomites point (Roghi et al.'s best age-constrained section) is a reference locality, hence the 5000 km uncertainty. Lu et al. note that the cause-effect chain with Wrangellia is not fully resolved and a local volcanic source is possible for their basin.
